issues.description: Inconsistent parameter types for PersonService.deletePerson across template, solution, and REST resource: the template (and the REST endpoint implementation) expect deletePerson to accept a UUID (personId) so PersonResource can call personService.deletePerson(personId), but the solution's PersonService declares deletePerson(Person) instead. This mismatch will cause compilation errors and prevents the REST delete endpoint from working as intended.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore consistency by making PersonService.deletePerson accept a UUID (personId) in the solution code (signature: public void deletePerson(UUID personId)) and implement removal by matching IDs. Alternatively, update PersonResource to pass a Person object (and retrieve it first) — but the simpler and intended fix is to change the service signature back to UUID to match the template and REST resource.

issues.description: The delete operation for Person is represented with different method signatures across artifacts: the template PersonService defines deletePerson(UUID personId) while the solution PersonService defines deletePerson(Person person). The REST endpoint described in the problem statement and implemented in PersonResource uses the personId path variable (UUID) and calls personService.deletePerson(personId). This mismatch (UUID vs Person parameter) is a semantic inconsistency that will confuse students about the expected service API and how the REST layer should delegate deletion, and can lead to compilation or usage errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the PersonService API so all artifacts use the same signature. Prefer using deletePerson(UUID personId) (service accepts the UUID) since the REST endpoint receives a personId path variable. Update the solution PersonService to provide deletePerson(UUID personId) (or overload it) and ensure PersonResource calls the matching method.
